text.p: Matches scheduled this week in the French first division (standings in parentheses, all kick-off times GMT):

Case of changing places as Montpellier look to remain unbeaten for 10th game in row after climbing out of relegation zone, while Lille, who won 1-0 at Montpellier in October but have taken only four points from seven games this year, slip deeper into mire despite win over Nancy in last home game.

Nantes have just overtaken Bordeaux in the standings and welcome back forward Claude Makelele from injury as they seek sixth away win in a row. Bordeaux have won three home games this year scoring 11 goals.

Monaco should bag another three points against bottom team to stay at least seven points clear at top. Nice have picked up only two points, both at home, in seven league games this year. Both Monaco's Laurent Viaud and Nice's Liberian striker James Debbah reportedly will be watched by England's Everton.

PSG's biggest test since visit to Monaco in January which ended in 2-0 defeat, they seem in better shape to face reigning champions after consecutive wins against AEK Athens and Metz with five goals from Patrice Loko. Auxerre, beaten 2-1 by Lens at weekend, still looking to bounce back from European Cup disappointment.

Corsicans will be looking to put challenge for European place back on rails after taking only one point from last three games. Cannes, who beat Rennes 1-0 at home on Saturday, should give young reserve keeper Sebastian Renaud second straight game after dropping Francois Lemasson after row with training staff.

Mid-table clash between sides virtually resigned to missing place in Europe, both victims of PSG revival having lost in last two matches played at Parc des Princes. Metz won last two home games against leaders Monaco and Lens.

Caen boosted hopes of surviving relegation by doing double over Marseille on Sunday with 1-0 home win after victory by same score at Velodrome in October. Strasbourg, who lost 3-0 at Caen in October, looking to recover from defeat at Guingamp.

Guingamp have discovered new striker in their Martinique-born midfielder Charles-Edouard Coridon, who scored both goals in 2-1 win over Strasbourg on Saturday. Le Havre are unbeaten at home this year.

Former European champions Marseille are at low ebb after mirage of 5-1 win over Lille last month. They have lost their last four matches and scored only once. Nancy have no away points or goals this year.

Lens boosted hopes of avoiding relegation with 2-1 home win over Auxerre on Saturday. Rennes' home form has dipped badly with two successive defeats after 12 games unbeaten and top scorer Stephane Guivarc'h is still goalless this year.
